stem:
For a class activity, Meera dips strips of dry turmeric paper into three colourless kitchen liquids: lemon juice (acidic), soap solution (basic), and plain water (neutral). She records what happens to each strip.

Which statement correctly describes what the turmeric paper test can and cannot show?

options.text: The paper turns red only in the soap solution, so Meera can identify the base but cannot tell the lemon juice and the plain water apart, as both leave the paper unchanged.
The paper turns red in the lemon juice, so Meera can use it to identify all three liquids separately.
The paper shows a different colour for each liquid, so turmeric paper works like a universal indicator.
The paper stays unchanged in the soap solution, so turmeric paper can only be used to detect acids.

teacher.key_rationale: Turmeric paper turns red in basic solutions only; acidic and neutral solutions both leave it unchanged, so it can identify the base but cannot distinguish an acid from a neutral substance. Option A states this diagnostic limit correctly. B and C overstate its resolving power; D reverses the response.
